title_en: The machine, files and the terminal: from the byte to the first pipeline (part 1 of 2)
how_to_read: sentences[].w = first..last word id inside this chapter; word k (0-based) of the sentence is first+k and `ar` is the spoken text (its space-separated tokens are those words); fr = [start_frame, end_frame] at 24 fps from the word map; impact = hook words (id=text); num = spoken numbers with data-contract fact ids; first_mention = glossary terms to chip (id=term); dup = same claim in another chapter. Anchor with {word, lead_frames} only. Visual candidates are ideas, never footage.

constraints.anchors: {word, lead_frames} only; never seconds or frames; event frame = word start - lead_frames
constraints.lead_frames: kinetic word -3, graphic state change -2, shot cut -4..-6 (inside a pause >= 200 ms), counter starts at the number word
constraints.density: >= 20 events/min; no gap > 4 s without an event (hold <= 6 s with reason); shot median 6-12 s, max 25 s (shots > 12 s: an event every 3 s)
constraints.coverage: every sentence >= 1 anchored event; >= 80 % of sentences a mechanism event; every spoken number and every first-mention term on screen
constraints.kinetic: 8-20 kinetic words per minute; <= 6 words and <= 2 lines on screen; impact word 1-2 words
constraints.fx: hero (real-time 3D) <= 5 % of chapter frames (ADR-002 RT5); fx_tier lite|standard|hero
constraints.text: text on busy backgrounds needs a plate or halo; sizes and safe areas: 04 sections 3.2 and 3.4
banned: invented numbers (every number: data-contract id or source sentence)
constraints.components: use only frozen components (harness/schemas/components/); requests go to corpus/specs/_component_requests.jsonl
constraints.chapter_rhythm: problem -> mental model -> progressive visual -> worked example -> prediction -> failure (crit) -> fix (ok) -> callback -> artifact (per chapter, not per sentence)

storyboard_notes.text: Micro-dive (1.8 min): use the consistent 'side note' card treatment (same card grammar every time).

sentences.ar: إحنا النهار ده هنغوص جوا أسرار المكنة بتاعتنا وهنفك طلاسم المعمارية بتاعتها من أول الـbits الصغيرين خالص لحد ما نبني مع بعض أول data pipeline.
sentences.en: Today we dive into the secrets of our machine and unravel its architecture, from the tiniest bits up to building our first data pipeline together.

sentences.ar: الشرح ده متصمم بالذات عشان يشيل أي غموضة عن الكمبيوتر ونتكلم عن الأساسيات اللي بتمشي عليها كل الداتا بتاعتنا.
sentences.en: This explainer is designed to remove any mystery about the computer and cover the basics all our data runs on.

sentences.ar: رحلتنا مترتبة زمنياً كالتالي هنبدأ من أساسيات الـhardware يعني من الـCPU للميموري
sentences.en: Our journey is ordered as follows: we start with hardware basics, from the CPU to memory,

sentences.ar: وبعدين الديتا والـbits الملفات والمسارات الامر الـterminal الـpipes ونختم بطريقة حل المشاكل وتجهيز بيئة العمل
sentences.en: then data and bits, files and paths, terminal commands, pipes, and we finish with troubleshooting and setting up the work environment.

sentences.ar: طيب أول محطة لنا المكنة نفسها من أول الـCPU لحد الميموري
sentences.en: OK, our first stop is the machine itself, from the CPU to memory.

sentences.ar: الـinstruction pointer بتاع الـCPU بيتحرك ويعمل الخطوات دي كل 700 ملي ثانية تقريبا
sentences.en: The CPU's instruction pointer moves and performs these steps roughly every 700 milliseconds.

sentences.ar: يعني أي برنامج شغال مش سحر خالص هو ببساطة عملية أو process بيديرها نظام التشغيل والـCPU بيمشي عليها خطوة خطوة
sentences.en: So any running program is not magic at all; it is simply a process managed by the operating system, and the CPU walks through it step by step.

sentences.ar: على الناحية الثانية بقى الـdisk عامل زي بلاطة بعيدة شوية وأبطأ بكتير
sentences.en: On the other side, the disk is like a slab a bit farther away, and much slower.

sentences.ar: القراية منه بالـmicroseconds أو الـmilliseconds بس بيحتفظ بالداتا بشكل دائم
sentences.en: Reading from it takes microseconds or milliseconds, but it keeps the data permanently.

sentences.ar: لو ركزنا مع عداد الـlatency اللي عمال يزيد مع المسافة ده هنفهم ليه بنقابل مشاكل في الأداء
sentences.en: If we watch the latency counter rising with distance, we understand why we run into performance problems.

sentences.ar: القسم الثاني خلونا نغوص في المستوى المايكروسكوبي شوية للـbits
sentences.en: Section two: let's dive a little into the microscopic level of bits.
Section two: data, bytes and encoding.

sentences.ar: ونسأل نفسنا سؤال التوقع ده كلمة café متكونة من 4 حروف بس
sentences.en: And ask ourselves this prediction question: the word café has only 4 letters.

sentences.ar: تفتكروا هتاخد كام byte عشان تتخزن فكروا فيها لحظة كده
sentences.en: How many bytes do you think it takes to store? Think about it for a moment.

sentences.ar: المفاجأة بقى إنها 5 bytes مش 4 خالص
sentences.en: The surprise is that it's 5 bytes, not 4 at all.

sentences.ar: رقم 5 ده بيشرح لنا فكرة الـencoding بمنتهى البساطة
sentences.en: This number 5 explains the idea of encoding very simply.

sentences.ar: في نظام UTF-8 الحرف اللي عليه علامة زي الـé بيحتاج 2 bytes عشان يتخزن مش byte 1
sentences.en: In UTF-8, an accented letter like é needs 2 bytes to be stored, not 1 byte.

facts.rule: A number goes on screen with its fact id as `ref`/`data_refs`. `unmatched_numbers` are spoken but have no data-contract fact: their source is the sentence itself (a valid `s:` ref); never replace them with a different figure.

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.
glossary.on_screen: Western digits, Latin terms in LTR isolates, Egyptian Arabic copy (no MSA), no per-letter animation (04 section 3.4).

concepts.def_en: The time between sending a request and receiving the response; usually tracked as percentiles such as p95, not just averages.

components.does: One whole word (or a tatweel-joined compound like الـKafka) on screen; never split per letter.
Up to 6 kinetic words on at most 2 lines, each word arriving on its own spoken word anchor.
A technical term chip (Latin in an LTR isolate) with an optional Arabic gloss; 28 px floor if spoken.
A counter that rolls from the previous value to the target over the spoken number (preset count).
An arrow from a label to a target layer (or a named part of it, 'layer.part').
Failure beat: glitch + low thud; flashes stay <= 3/s (WCAG 2.3.1).
Fix beat: the target settles into place with a settle chime.
The shot camera: move + ease + intensity; drift always on; optional impact nudges (<= 4 px) on anchors.
Match cut between a layer of this shot and one of the next.
Lower-third caption for a source, term, speaker or location.
Draw an SVG path (stroke reveal; RTL by default for Arabic layouts).
A tree as a flat parent list: variant btree | plan | decision | fs.
A terminal (LTR isolate) whose lines appear on anchors.
Roles x resources with grant levels; locks deny or open.
Nodes sending heartbeats; a missed beat marks a node suspect.
Scrolling log lines (LTR isolate) by level.
Deep-Dive entry card with parent chapter and prerequisite concepts.
